To create a permanently shared directory using Samba and connectable under Windows, you can follow these steps:

1. Install the Samba package on your Ubuntu system by running `sudo apt-get install samba`.
2. Create a new directory that you want to share.
3. Edit the Samba configuration file by running `sudo nano /etc/samba/smb.conf`.
4. Add the following lines at the end of the file:
```
[shared_directory]
  path = /path/to/shared/directory
  browseable = yes
  writable = yes
  force user = nobody
```
Replace `/path/to/shared/directory` with the actual path to the directory you want to share.

5. Save and close the file.
6. Restart the Samba service by running `sudo service samba restart`.
7. On your Windows system, open File Explorer and navigate to `\\[your-ubuntu-system-name]\shared_directory`.

Note: Make sure to replace `[your-ubuntu-system-name]` with the actual name of your Ubuntu system.

To control credentials management on your Samba server under Ubuntu, you can follow these steps:

1. Install the Samba package on your Ubuntu system by running `sudo apt-get install samba`.
2. Configure Samba share access controls by managing user authentication, permissions, and security options for shared directories.
3. Use the smb.conf file to configure Samba settings, including authentication and authorization.
4. Implement identity mapping backends, such as rid and autorid, to manage user identities.
5. Choose an identity mapping backend based on your specific needs.

You can find more information in the Ubuntu Server Guide at https://ubuntu.com/server/docs/how-to/Samba/file-server-print-server-share-access-controls-and-more.
